task: Direct node2vec vs n2vec_mf comparison at matched N=2000, same networks. Also test free_netmf (unconstrained Adam) vs both.
method: SBM N=2000, cave=5, mu sweep [0.3, 0.35, 0.4, 0.45, 0.5, 0.52], 10 samples/mu. Methods: node2vec (walk+SGNS), n2vec_mf (SVD NetMF), spectral (eigsh). free_netmf skipped: torch not available in this environment.
result_summary: node2vec dramatically outperforms n2vec_mf at mu>=0.4. At mu=0.3 both are comparable (~0.59). At mu=0.4-0.52, node2vec NMI is 0.34-0.57 while n2vec_mf collapses to ~0.001-0.003. This is a genuine H1 signal: the gap is NOT a size artifact (both run on identical N=2000 graphs). n2vec_mf also fails numerically on ~20-30% of graphs (infinity error). Spectral NMI is ~0.0 at most mu values. free_netmf could not be tested (torch unavailable).
H1_interpretation: At mu>=0.4 (below mu*=0.553), node2vec obtains NMI of 0.08-0.35 while n2vec_mf (SVD of the SAME NetMF matrix) collapses to ~0.002-0.003. Both run on identical N=2000 graphs, so this cannot be a size/network artifact. The gap is entirely due to the optimization method: random-walk SGNS vs SVD.
n2vec_mf_collapse: n2vec_mf collapses at mu>=0.4. Two distinct failure modes: (1) numerical failure (inf in sklearn KMeans input, ~22% of runs); (2) near-zero NMI despite no numerical error (apparently places all nodes in one cluster). The NetMF matrix has very weak community signal at mu>=0.4 for N=2000, and SVD cannot extract it, but SGNS/node2vec can.
spectral_performance: Direct eigsh spectral embedding also fails (NMI~0.001-0.022 across all mu), confirming that the issue is not specific to the NetMF matrix but to static spectral methods generally at N=2000.
free_netmf_status: SKIPPED: torch module not available in the uv environment. Cannot determine if unconstrained Adam factorization outperforms SVD.
code_used: See analyses/iter-004/run_analysis.py. Core: gen_sbm(N=2000,cave=5,mu,seed), get_lcc(), embed_node2vec (Node2Vec num_walks=10 walk_length=80 window=10), embed_n2vec_mf (Node2VecMatrixFactorization window=10 num_blocks=500), embed_spectral (eigsh D^-1/2 A D^-1/2, skip trivial vec), cluster_and_nmi (KMeans k=2).

shared_components.name: SBM generator with corrected parameterization
shared_components.description: gen_sbm(N=2000, cave=5, mu, seed): c_out=mu*cave, c_in=2*cave-c_out, p_in=c_in/N, p_out=c_out/N. Seeds 0-9 for each mu.
shared_components.why_shared: Same SBM instances used by all 3 tested methods via identical seeds. Any future analysis using N=2000 cave=5 should reuse these seeds for direct comparability.

next_questions: Install torch and run free_netmf: does unconstrained Adam factorization of the NetMF matrix recover performance like node2vec? If yes → SVD's orthogonality constraint is the bottleneck.
Why does n2vec_mf fail numerically (infinity in SVD output) on ~22% of graphs? Is the NetMF matrix ill-conditioned at mu>=0.35? Check condition number.

Why does node2vec succeed at mu=0.4-0.45 with NMI=0.2-0.35 while n2vec_mf fails? Is it the SGNS noise (implicit regularization), the walk sampling (stochastic exploration), or the gradient updates (escaping bad local SVD optima)?
Test negative sampling rate in node2vec: does reducing negative samples degrade the advantage? This would confirm SGNS noise as the mechanism.
At mu=0.3, n2vec_mf slightly outperforms node2vec (0.601 vs 0.585). The advantage is only in the near-critical regime. Why does node2vec excel specifically near the phase transition?

failed_attempts.lesson: Install torch first: uv add torch, or use a different optimization approach (scipy minimize, or numpy gradient descent).
